status: discussion proposal; not a production metric

definitions.channels: Recording channels digitized at the same time in the described configuration.
definitions.sample_rate_hz: Per-channel sampling rate of the described configuration.
definitions.adc_bits: Bits per sample as stated by the source. null when the source read here does not state it.
definitions.raw_rate_bit_s_derived: channels x sample_rate_hz x adc_bits. DERIVED by this proposal, not reported by the source. Payload only: no framing, line code or protocol overhead. null when any factor is null.
definitions.raw_rate_reported: The source's own statement of generated data rate, verbatim, when it gives one.
definitions.link_rate_bit_s: Data rate of the link that carries data out of the body or off the head, as stated by the source. null for wired systems and when not stated.
definitions.power_mw: Power as stated by the source. power_scope says what the number covers. Scopes differ between records and are not comparable without care.
definitions.raw_rate_bit_s_reported: The source's own statement of generated data rate as a number, when it gives one in bit/s. raw_rate_reported keeps the wording.
definitions.requirement: A stated design requirement or target. Not an observation; never plotted as a measurement.

records.label: Simeral et al. 2021, two pedestal-mounted Brown Wireless Devices
records.channels_basis: '192-electrode iBCI'; 'two 96-channel intracortical arrays', one transmitter per array
records.link: radio at 3.3 or 3.5 GHz, Manchester encoded
records.link_rate_qualifier: not stated in the main text read here; Supplemental Table SI was not read. A university news release says 'two devices used together recorded neural signals at 48 megabits per second from 200 electrodes', which does not match this row's 192 channels and is kept as context only.

excerpts: we replaced the external cables of a 192-electrode iBCI with wireless transmitters

The BWD applies a hardware filter (1 Hz to 7.8 kHz), digitizes neural activity (20 kS/sec, 12 bits per sample) on each electrode, applies Manchester encoding and transmits it to nearby antennas using a custom low-power protocol.
Transmission frequency was configurable such that neural activity from two 96-channel intracortical arrays could be recorded simultaneously without interference.
two devices used together recorded neural signals at 48 megabits per second from 200 electrodes with a battery life of over 36 hours

records.label: Neuralink N1, as stated on the company's compression challenge page
records.subjects: non-human primate (the data on that page)
records.link_rate_qualifier: approximate ('~1Mbps'), company statement on a web page, not a peer-reviewed measurement
records.date_basis: archived copy dated 2024-06-01; the live URL returned 'NoSuchKey' (404) on 2026-11-20

excerpts: Compression is essential: N1 implant generates ~200Mbps of eletrode data (1024 electrodes @ 20kHz, 10b resolution) and can transmit ~1Mbps wirelessly. So > 200x compression is needed. Compression must run in real time (< 1ms) at low power (< 10mW, including radio).

records.requirement: 'Compression must run in real time (< 1ms) at low power (< 10mW, including radio)' and '> 200x compression is needed'

records.label: WIMAGINE (Mestais et al. 2015), 32-channel streaming configuration
records.form: active implantable device, powered by an inductive link
records.channels_basis: The implant has 64 electrodes. The paper states 'Either up to 32 channels can be transmitted with a sampling frequency of 1 kHz or up to 64 channels with a sampling frequency of 600 Hz.' This record is the 32-channel case.
records.link_rate_qualifier: measured effective throughput at up to 2 m

excerpts: The wireless transmission of the raw recorded neural signals requires a high throughput of approximately 400 kb/s for the transmission of 32 channels sampled at 976 Hz on 12 bits.
An effective data throughput of 450 kb/s between the implant and the base station was measured over several hours at a distance of 2 m.
The bottleneck of the WIMAGINE acquisition system is the wireless data rate.
In any case, the maximum power consumption is 75 mW.

records.label: Paradromics Connexus, one cortical module (SONIC preprint)
records.sample_rate_basis: the rate used in this study; the source says the module 'provides a tunable sampling rate'
records.link_rate_qualifier: upper bound ('supporting speeds of up to 100 Mbps')

excerpts: amplified and bandpass filtered between ~10 Hz and 2.2 kHz through a multi-stage analog hardware pipeline before digitization at a 5.2 kHz sampling rate
The IT distributes power to the Cortical Module and transmits neural data wirelessly through the skin to the ET via a secure near-infrared optical link, supporting speeds of up to 100 Mbps.

context_sources.label: Even-Chen et al. 2020, Nature Biomedical Engineering
excerpts: The efficacy of wireless intracortical brain-computer interfaces (iBCIs) is limited in part by the number of recording channels, which is constrained by the power budget of the implantable system.
In contrast to the conventional system, whose power consumption would be limited by the transmitter (50-93%), the proposed design's power consumption is limited by the neural amplifier (92%).
